items.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998
items.q: I played for Milton Berle, who had a lot of music, as does Don Rickles.

ctx.x: Did you ever have any train wrecks along the way, that maybe necessarily weren’t your fault, but something happened?
I can remember breaking a drum head. I played for Milton Berle, who had a lot of music, as does Don Rickles. Comedians tend to have a lot of music. And he wanted a big rim

shot right at the beginning. And we practiced this rim shot during rehearsal. So I thought, boy it he going to get a rim shot, in a packed showroom. And I came from above my head with the butt of the stick, and came down on that drum head, and there was no saving it. I split the head completely across, which — no sound at all. And the only method I could think to get through the show was I turned the drum over and played on the bottom head, and I broke that too, because the bottom head is significantly thinner…
